content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to increase/decrease a value using [product_name] with [article_no] hardware, but when I use a Timer [on-delay] and attempt to set the reference to a Counter [up/down counter], there is no reference option in [article_no]. If I switch hardware (using Ctrl-H) to [article_no] or [article_no], it becomes possible to use a reference. Does anyone know why this is happening? Best regards, enjoy the holidays [user_name]

Hi, There are several posts in the forum addressing this issue. [url] In [product_name] version [version_no], reference connections are handled graphically, similar to signal wiring. You can open the parameter box (by clicking the plus sign) on both function blocks and then wire the reference between them. In the tool's color settings, you can also assign a different color to the referencing wire. Hope this helps.

I understand now! Thank you so much. After looking for a while, I missed it, even after searching the forum. I figured it out eventually (after three days of trying!). Thanks again. Best regards, [user_name]
A new question published by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread with the subject 'guide me to be a good user.' Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced confusion when trying to set a reference from a Timer [on-delay] to a Counter [up/down counter] in [article_no] hardware, as the method was different compared to previous versions. The updated approach requires graphical wiring instead of selecting a reference from a dropdown menu, leading to difficulties and uncertainty. Users needed additional guidance to learn the new method, highlighting a need for better visibility and clearer instructions within the tool when workflows change.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reference connections to work consistently across hardware versions, or for any changes to be clearly indicated within the software interface. They want to be able to easily discover how to create references and receive guidance if the method has changed.
